Rashi on Niddah 30b:10:1.english: A purgative medicine - A medicine through which she miscarries and scatters any seed that [was] in the womb beforehand.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:13:1.english: [She] transferred them to a steward - so that no man had intercourse with them except [on] that day.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:14:1.hebrew: ודילמא אי קרעוה כו' - לרבי ישמעאל פריך. נהי נמי דלשומר מסרינהו, אפ"ה מנלן שלא נוצרה נקבה עד פ"א? דילמא אי קרעוה להך ליום מ"א, הוה משתכחא:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:14:1.english: And perhaps if they had torn [her] open, etc. - He is raising an objection against Rabbi Yishmael: Even though they handed them over to a guard, nevertheless, from where do we know that a female [embryo] is not formed until [day] eighty-one? Perhaps if they had torn open this [woman] on day forty-one, it would have been found.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:14:2.hebrew: בסימניהון שוין - נקבה שנמצא ליום פ"א, לא היו אבריה ושערה וצפורניה אלא כשיעור של זכר ליום מ"א:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:14:2.english: Their indications were identical - [The] female [embryo] that was found on the eighty-first day, its limbs, its hair, and its fingernails were only like the measure of a male [embryo] on the forty-first day.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:15:1.hebrew: היינו ת"ק - דתנא לעיל: "ליום מ"א תשב לזכר ולנקבה ולנדה", אלמא בריית נקבה ליום מ"א:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:15:1.english: [It] is identical to the first tanna - For [the Mishnah] taught above: "On the forty-first day, she sits [in impurity] for a male, and for a female, and for a menstruant"; thus, the formation of a female [concludes] on the forty-first day.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:16:1.hebrew: וכי תימא - רישא להכי תנא ליה לאשמועינן סתמא דמתניתין כרבנן, ונשמע מינה דהלכתא כוותייהו. ולא נהירא לי גירסא ופירושה, דה"ל סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת, ואין הלכה כסתם. ונ"ל דהכי גרס: וכי תימא למסתמא כרבנן, ויחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים — פשיטא, מהו דתימא כו'. והכי פירושה: וכי תימא תנא הך סיפא לאשמעינן דסתמא דלעיל סתמא דרבנן היא, ויחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים — פשיטא דסתמא דרבים היא, הואיל וסתמא תנייה רבי, ולא אשכחן יחידאה דאמר הכי דנימא פלוני היא:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:16:1.english: And if you would say - [some explain that] the first clause was taught for this [purpose]: to teach us [that] the unattributed [ruling] of the Mishnah is in accordance with the Rabbis, and we would infer from it that the halakha is in accordance with them. However, neither [this] textual reading nor its explanation appears plausible to me, for it would be an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute, and the halakha is not in accordance with an unattributed [ruling in such a case]. Rather, it appears to me that the text should read thus: "And if you would say, to establish it anonymously in accordance with the Rabbis, and [when there is a dispute between] an individual and the majority, the halakha is in accordance with the majority — it is obvious! What might you have said, etc." And this is its explanation: And if you would say [that] he taught this latter clause to teach us that the unattributed [ruling] above is the unattributed [opinion] of the Rabbis, and [when there is a dispute between] an individual and the majority, the halakha is in accordance with the majority — it is obvious that it is the unattributed [opinion] of the majority, since Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] taught it anonymously, and we have not found an individual [Sage] who said thus, such that we would say it is [the opinion of] so-and-so.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:17:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא כו' - קמשמע לן, מדמהדר רבי ושנאה בלשון חכמים, שמע מינה דהלכה כסתם ראשון, ואף על פי שמחלוקת ר' ישמעאל בצדו:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:17:1.english: Lest you say, etc. - It teaches us [that] since Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] went back and taught it in the phrasing of "the Sages," learn from it that the halakha is in accordance with the first anonymous [teaching], even though the dispute of Rabbi Yishmael is alongside it.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:18:1.english: A notebook - Tablets on which the priests write.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:18:3.english: Lest it kill its mother - For the womb is not wide [enough] to expel excrement that accumulates in it.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:1:1.hebrew: הא קתני נדה - דכל דמים שתראה, טמאים. ומשני: לכך הוזכר זכר, שאם תראה ליום ל"ד ותחזור ותראה ליום מ"א, תהא מקולקלת עד מ"ח. שכשראתה ליום ל"ד ללידתה, אמרינן טמאה, אע"ג דאכתי משכי ימי טוהר דזכר, מספקינן לה בלא ולד ותשב לנדה. וכי הדר חזיא ליום מ"א, שהוא ח' לראייתה, ותרצה להיות שומרת יום כנגד יום — אמרינן: ולד היה וזכר היה, וראייה דיום ל"ד דם טוהר היא, והשתא הוא דהויא תחלת נדה. והשתא מקלקלינן לה דלא טבלה עד מ"ח, שהוא ח' לראייה אחרונה. ואי לאו משום ספקא דזכר, הוה טבלה למחר ליום מ"ב, ממ"נ: אי לאו ולד הוא — הרי שומרת יום כנגד יום היא, ואי ולד הוא ונקבה היא — אכתי הוה דם טוהר עד שמונים; וספקא דזכר מקלקלא לה:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:1:1.english: Doesn't [the mishna] teach [the strictures of] a menstruating woman - That all blood that she sees [is] impure. And [the Gemara] answers: For this [reason] a male was mentioned, that if she sees [blood] on the thirty-fourth day and again sees [blood] on the forty-first day, she shall be ruined [in her purity status] until the forty-eighth [day]. For when she saw [blood] on the thirty-fourth day from her birth, we say [she is] impure; even though the days of purity of a male still extend [beyond then], we treat her as uncertain [that perhaps there was] no child, and she must observe [the days of] a menstruating woman. And when she sees [blood] again on the forty-first day, which is the eighth [day] from her [first] sighting, and she wants to be a woman who observes a day against a day — we say: There was a child and it was a male, and the sighting of the thirty-fourth day was blood of purity, and now is when the beginning of [her] menstruation is. And now we ruin [her purity status] so that she does not immerse until the forty-eighth [day], which is the eighth [day] from the last sighting. And if not for the uncertainty of a male, she would immerse tomorrow, on the forty-second day, in either case: if it was not a child — behold, she is a woman who observes a day against a day; and if it was a child and it was a female — it is still blood of purity until eighty [days]; and thus the uncertainty of a male ruins [her purity status].

Rashi on Niddah 30b:21:1.hebrew: ת"ש בסוד אלוה עלי אהלי - והא אוקמיה בירחי לידה, מדכתיב "כירחי קדם":
Rashi on Niddah 30b:21:1.english: Come and hear: "When the converse of God was upon my tent" - For [the Gemara] already established [this passage as referring] to the months of gestation, since it is written, "as in the months of old."

Rashi on Niddah 30b:24:1.hebrew: ולא נשבע למרמה - שקיים שבועתו לשמור את התורה, דאי בשבועה בעלמא, אטו משום דלא נשבע למרמה חשיב להו בעולין בהר ה':
Rashi on Niddah 30b:24:1.english: And has not sworn deceitfully - [Meaning] that he fulfilled his oath to keep the Torah; for if [it referred] to an ordinary oath, is it merely because he did not swear deceitfully that [Scripture] counts them among those who ascend the mountain of the Lord?

Rashi on Niddah 30b:3:1.english: And similarly, with regard to a female - That is to say, the uncertainty of a female [birth] also ruins her [status with] this ruination.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:3:2.hebrew: עד פ"ח - דלא טבלה עד פ"ח, דאי הוה פשיטא לן דלאו ולד הוא, הואי טבלה למחר ביום פ"ב, דראיית פ"א באחד עשר יום שבין נדה לנדה היא. ומשום דמספקא לן דילמא ולד הוה, וראייה דיום ע"ד דם טהור הוה, והשתא הויא תחלת נדה, לא טבלה עד פ"ח:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:3:2.english: Until [the] eighty-eighth [day] - For she cannot immerse until [day] eighty-eight, for if it were clear to us that it was not a fetus, she would immerse on the next day, on day eighty-two, because the sighting of [day] eighty-one is within the eleven days that are between one niddah [period] and [another] niddah [period]. And because we are in doubt [that] perhaps it was a fetus, and the sighting of day seventy-four was pure blood, and now it is the beginning of niddah, she cannot immerse until [day] eighty-eight.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:4:1.hebrew: טימא וטיהר בזכר - מ' יום בין שתיהן, ז' לטומאה ול"ג יום לימי טוהר:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:4:1.english: [The verse] deemed [her] impure and deemed [her] pure in [the case of] a male - Forty days between both of them: seven [days] for impurity, and thirty-three days for the days of purity.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:6:1.hebrew: נתחייבו הריגה - ומתוך שעומדות ליהרג, ניסו בהם ויחדום לביאה, וקרעו שתיהם לסוף מ', ונמצא אחד זכר ואחד נקבה:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:6:1.english: They were sentenced to death - And since they were about to be executed, they experimented on them and designated them for intercourse; and they cut open both of them at the end of forty [days], and one was found [to be] a male and one a female.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:8:1.hebrew: תלד - דאם נקבה תלד (ויקרא י״ב:ה׳) קרא יתירא הוא, דמצי למכתב "ואם נקבה וטמאה שבועים", דהא כתיב לעיל "וילדה זכר":
Rashi on Niddah 30b:8:1.english: She gives birth - For [the phrase] "if she gives birth to a female" (Leviticus 12:5) is a superfluous verse, as it could have written "and if a female, then she shall be impure two weeks," since it is written above "and she gives birth to a male."

Rashi on Niddah 30b:9:1.hebrew: מקמי זכר - ואף ע"ג שיחדום לבעול ביום אחד, שמא מעוברת היתה קודם לכן:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:9:1.english: Before a male - And even though they secluded them to have intercourse on the same day, perhaps she was [already] pregnant before then.

Tosafot on Niddah 30b:13:1.hebrew: שומר גופיה בא עליה - ואפילו היה סריס או אשה, אפשר שהניח אחרים לבא:
Tosafot on Niddah 30b:13:1.english: [The] warden himself engaged in intercourse with her - And even if [the warden] was a eunuch or a woman, it is possible that [the warden] allowed others to engage in intercourse [with her].

Tosafot on Niddah 30b:16:1.hebrew: וכי תימא למיסתמא כרבנן - ואע"ג דרישא נמי סתמא קתני, לא חשיב סתמא כיון דפליג עליה רבי ישמעאל, והוי אדרבה סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת, כדאמרינן בהחולץ (יבמות מב:):
Tosafot on Niddah 30b:16:1.english: "And if you would say [that the purpose is] to [teach] the unattributed [opinion] in accordance with the Rabbis" - Even though the first clause is also taught unattributed, it is not considered an unattributed [mishna], since Rabbi Yishmael disputes it; on the contrary, it is [a case of] an unattributed [statement] followed by a dispute, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 42b).

Tosafot on Niddah 30b:18:1.hebrew: שני אציליו על שני ארכובותיו - פ"ה: איישילי"ש. ור"ת פירש דאציל היינו קוד"א, דאמר בפ' האומר משקלי (ערכין יט:): "משקל ידי עלי, משקל רגלי עלי כו'", ומכניס ידו עד האציל ורגלו עד הארכובה; וקוד"א ביד הוא כנגד הארכובה ברגל. ועוד, דהתם משמע דאציל הוא מרפק, ובאהלות (פ"א מ"ח) משמע — שמנה לפי סדרי אברי האדם — דמרפק היינו קוד"א. ועוד אמר בפ"ב דזבחים (דף יח:): "לא יחגרו ביזע" — שאין חוגרין אלא כנגד אצילי ידיהם, והיינו כנגד הקוד"א שדרך העולם לחגור; ובבית השחי, אדרבה, שם הוא מקום זיעה:
Tosafot on Niddah 30b:18:1.english: Its two arms [atzilav] on its two knees - Rashi explains [atzil as] aiseles [armpits]. And Rabbeinu Tam explained that atzil is coude [elbow], for it says in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer Mishkali (Arakhin 19b): "[If one says,] 'The weight of my hand is upon me,' [or] 'The weight of my foot is upon me,' etc.," and he inserts his hand up to the atzil and his foot up to the knee; and the coude on the arm corresponds to the knee on the leg. Furthermore, there it implies that atzil is marpek, and in Ohalot (1:8) it implies — as it lists [the limbs] according to the order of the limbs of a person — that marpek is coude. Furthermore, it says in the second chapter of Zevachim (18b): "They shall not gird themselves in sweat" [Ezekiel 44:18] — for they only gird themselves opposite the atzilei of their hands, and that is opposite the coude, where it is the way of the world to gird; whereas in the armpit, on the contrary, that is a place of sweat.
